subject: Post-demo recap: routing & capacity economics — options and asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchidai.com>, Tom Ridge <tom.ridge@orchidai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: routing & capacity economics — options and asks

Hi Samir / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time today — really helpful to see the latency-sensitive routing you described for search ranking + the batch embedding pipeline for analytics. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on economics and a light procurement path: 

1) Quick recap of deployment fits: 
- Hosted API: lowest friction and fastest time-to-value for proof-of-concept (no infra to stand up). Good if you expect <100 qps peak and can tolerate per-token pricing.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): better unit cost and predictable throughput for sustained traffic (~100–1,000 qps). Requires commit (monthly/annual).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): recommended if you need private networking, KMS/HSM integration, or strict data residency. Higher setup and support overhead.

2) Economics asks (so we can build a comparison table):
- Current and expected token throughput (monthly average and peak). If you can share a 90-day pattern that would be ideal.
- Target latency SLO for the ranking path (p95 target).
- Any hard constraints on traffic location (must run in VPC in us-west vs acceptable in our hosted eu region).

3) Next steps I propose: 
- You share weekly token/req profile and any regulatory constraints (Elena or procurement can send).
- We build two scenarios by Friday: (A) Hosted API ramp (per-token) with caching + prefix KV savings; (B) Dedicated commit estimate including burst allowance and tooling cost. I’ll cc Marissa and Ben to produce a light TCO and architecture note.

Attaching a short two-page scenarios doc and a draft MPA with high-level terms. Happy to jump on a follow-up call after you check numbers.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0148

Attachment stubs: redwood-deploy-econ-scenarios-3page.pdf (pdf), orchard-mpa-draft-terms.docx (docx)
From: Samir Patel <samir@orchidai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@orchidai.com>, Tom Ridge <tom.ridge@orchidai.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Aug 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: routing & capacity economics — options and asks

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers and a couple of follow-ups so your team can model realistic numbers: 

- Throughput: current prod is ~3M tokens/day (spikes to ~250k tokens/hour during batch refresh windows). For the search ranking path, we expect ~40 qps during business hours, spikes ~180 qps during PR/marketing events. Long term (Q4) planning target is 2–3x that.
- Latency: p95 target for ranking responses is 120ms. For embeddings batch, throughput >1k recs/min is fine since it’s async.
- Data residency: primary requirement is all ranking inference for European users must stay within eu-west region. We have a shortlist of vendors in EMEA. For now, US traffic can run in hosted.

Elena from procurement will send over current contract playbook and a PoC purchase order template we use for pilots. Also can you clarify how fallbacks would work if Dedicated capacity hits saturation (do you have automatic routing to hosted variants and what are the latency implications)?

Thanks —
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Engineering | OrchidAI
samir@orchidai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Aug 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: routing & capacity economics — options and asks

Jonas / team — forwarding Samir's throughput/latency numbers. Ben/Karthik can you start sketching two scenarios: 

A) Hosted API ramp: assumptions we should use: 3M tokens/day baseline, monthly growth 10%, caching reduces token counts by ~18% for the ranking prefix, and p95 target 120ms. Provide expected monthly $/month and per-response median cost. 

B) Dedicated 3x GPU reserved pool: include commit levels (monthly and annual), estimated amortized infra cost, expected token-equivalent break-even point, and notes on autoscale/burst cost. Also include EMEA replica cost for region constraints.

Please add a short note on how automatic fallback to hosted would be handled and estimated latency delta (will need this for procurement).

Marissa
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchidai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@orchidai.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: routing & capacity economics — options and asks

Hi Samir / Elena —

Attached is a short scenarios packet: redwood-deploy-econ-scenarios-3page.pdf (overview, hosted vs dedicated cost table, break-even math) and a draft MPA with pilot terms (orchidai-mpa-draft-terms.docx). High-level summary here: 

- Hosted baseline (monthly, assumed 90-day smoothing): ~$5,200/month for current 3M token/day profile with caching applied. This assumes no reserved commit and standard per-token rates; predictable but higher marginal cost as volume grows.

- Dedicated reserve (3-GPU pool, monthly commit): ~$12,000/month amortized (incl. infra + managed support) with break-even at ~9M tokens/day equivalent given your latency SLOs and caching. Adding an EMEA replica increases commit to ~$18,000/month. Annual commit reduces unit cost by ~18%.

- Fallbacks: We support policy-based routing. If Dedicated at customer pool is saturated, requests can be routed to a compatible hosted model variant automatically. Typical p95 increase observed is +40–80ms depending on region egress; we can configure cold-warm KV replication to minimize penalty for ranking paths. These fallbacks are enabled by default in our managed playbook and can be tuned per route.

Next asks from OrchidAI: procurement PO template and any required security questionnaire fields. We will incorporate Elena’s procurement notes into the formal pricing doc.

If helpful, happy to do a 30-minute walk-through of the PDF and commit math tomorrow.

—Ben
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
